components.label: The latch, where demonstrated and where needed
components.note: Real in conduit arteries (VASO-C010: VASO-E003) but not generic across vascular smooth muscle (VASO-E021 on VASO-C010). In the compartment the thesis names, pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained activation, not a latch (VASO-E020 on VASO-C020), no arteriole's energetic cost has been measured (VASO-E019 on VASO-C020), and no latch has been identified at any tender point (VASO-E016 on VASO-C020). A mismatch and a gap, not a refutation.

components.label: The breath key and the seconds-scale release
components.note: The felt release (VASO-C004) is proponent testimony (VASO-E014); the state-not-structure inference (VASO-C011) stands on priors with VASO-E030 showing only that measures move over visits. Slow breathing shifts autonomic balance globally (VASO-C013: VASO-E009). The two-key necessity (VASO-C039) has one record (VASO-E067) that establishes only that a pressure-only protocol omitted breathing instruction; the blood-first ordering (VASO-C073) is anchor-only. No time-resolved record exists in either direction.

components.label: Vascular memory and participation in mind
components.note: The read path exists as instantaneous modulation in rat brain (VASO-C012: VASO-E005; VASO-E004 as the hypothesis); attention can regulate a peripheral bed at a chosen site over tens of minutes (VASO-C006: VASO-E008, qualified by VASO-E041). The memory attribution (VASO-C021) is held on hypothesis statements (VASO-E013, VASO-E038) and fails the write–store–read test (VASO-E017); the contemplative-map identification (VASO-C022) has one uncited assertion behind it (VASO-E039).

components.label: The competing accounts: perforator and densification
components.note: The three-element perforator hold (VASO-C174), its skin-territory write (VASO-C143) and the reversibility of fascial densification (VASO-C077) are held on anchors alone — the first two in a source the ledger has not read — with no admitted observation for or against any of them. They are featured because each is a different mechanism with a cheap, specified test (VASO-R015, VASO-R017, VASO-R008), not because anything supports them.

researchPriority.reason: The decisive experiments are small, specified and unrun: a time-locked imaging study of a single release, and a breath-randomized repeat of a compression protocol that already exists. Either result in either direction would move the case verdict, and the cost is a small grant.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on hypothesis statements only: Johnson's three hypotheses (VASO-E013, context) and the founding essay's relay of the clinging-as-latch identification (VASO-E038, context). The critical report's qualifier (VASO-E017) states the operational criteria for memory — state depends on prior input, can be read out, discriminates between prior inputs — and finds the latch literature addresses none of them. No admitted record demonstrates a vascular state storing content that a later neural readout recovers.

treatment.plainLanguage: Held tension in blood-vessel walls works as a kind of memory the mind uses, and the mental grasping Buddhism calls clinging is physically a vascular hold.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If demonstrated, it would decide the case and establish a new memory mechanism; as it stands, no record moves it in either direction, so it contributes nothing to the present verdict.
treatment.strongestObjection: Hysteresis is not memory: a thermostat depends on its history without having an autobiography, and nothing in the latch literature shows content-specific write, storage and readback (VASO-E017).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: In an animal preparation with oxygenation clamped, different induced vascular states producing reliably different later neural responses to identical stimulation after the initiating input stops (VASO-R005).

Vascular manipulation altering neural gain only through instantaneous perfusion, with no history dependence once perfusion is equalized — which would collapse the claim to ordinary neurovascular physiology.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The supporting observations attached to this claim are consistent with it but not diagnostic: the Doppler high-resistance pattern (VASO-E027) is one whose authors list contracture compression as a co-equal cause and never mention latch, so it is weighed at zero diagnosticity. The undermining records are direct: the critical report's audit finds no study identifying smooth-muscle latch at any tender point (VASO-E016); pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising phosphorylation, not the dephosphorylated hold a latch requires (VASO-E020); no arteriole's energetic cost has ever been measured (VASO-E019). The proponent's own statement (VASO-E037) is a hypothesis statement at no weight; the second essay's relocation and concession (VASO-E044, VASO-E045) are drawn from a source the ledger has not read and are treated as absent. Neither direction holds time-resolved evidence, so unresolved rather than contradicted.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a small blood vessel inside the muscle held shut cheaply by its own smooth muscle, starving the tissue around it — a maintained state, not damaged tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis in its graded form; every rung below it either supports it non-diagnostically or, in the arteriole record, points away from it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Where the latch has actually been examined at arteriole caliber, constriction tracks maintained activation, and no study has found a latch at a tender point (VASO-E020, VASO-E016).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after its stimulus is withdrawn, at falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost (VASO-R004).
A palpated knot stiff on elastography, active on EMG and metabolically cold on FDG-PET (VASO-R013).
Time-resolved imaging of a release with perfusion rising before stiffness falls (VASO-R001); or, against it, elevated FDG uptake and the non-latching phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source (the proponent's second essay) that the ledger has not been able to read and verify. No admitted evidence record bears on it in either direction. It is featured as a genuinely different mechanism — an alternative to VASO-C021's single vascular memory element — with cheap specified tests.

treatment.plainLanguage: On the perforator picture, a knot is held by three things at once — the vessel's tone, a collar of gelled lubricant around the bundle, and the tether that collar makes to the fascial sheet — each of which stays put after the input that set it has gone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If tender points sit on Doppler-mapped perforators above chance and can be released by hydrodissection without breath, this account displaces the latch; a null coincidence map dissolves it.
treatment.strongestObjection: The one instrumented pattern the ledger holds — stiff regions blinded sonographers map in the trapezius and calf — lies inside the muscle, not in the fascia under the skin, and nothing admitted supports any of the three elements.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded pencil-Doppler map showing palpated tender points coincide with perforators above chance (VASO-R015).
Ultrasound-guided saline hydrodissection at a mapped perforator releasing a tender point with no breath and no pressure, against sham (VASO-R017).
Tender points falling on perforators no more often than chance.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The sole record (VASO-E039, weak) is the founding essay's uncited assertion that the traditional maps place knots along the torso midline and limbs, with no coding rule and no chance baseline. No blinded coding has been done; post-hoc matching cannot be excluded.

treatment.plainLanguage: The knots and channels of Tibetan, Indian and Chinese body maps are first-person charts of the same tension system, drawn by people with highly trained inner attention.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a genuine alignment of traditional knot locations with vascular geography would not show that anything latches or clenches; the claim rides on the mechanism claims rather than deciding them.
treatment.strongestObjection: Correspondence found after the fact is the weakest evidence there is, and no one has coded the traditional locations blind against chance.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Preregistered coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations aligning with vascular branch points, sympathetic chains or dense fascia above chance (VASO-R006).
The same coding finding no alignment beyond chance, which would retire the convergence argument.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The Hai–Murphy kinetic model (VASO-E003, strong) reproduces high sustained stress at low myosin phosphorylation — economical force maintenance after activation subsides — and is textbook physiology. The study table (VASO-E021) qualifies its generality: latch behaviour was present in the rabbit femoral artery and absent in its saphenous branch, and never followed further downstream. The essay's restatement (VASO-E034) adds nothing and overstates the model as force at zero activation; the model says low, not none.

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle in vessel walls can lock its grip and hold tension cheaply for a long time after the signal that started it has faded.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Established physiology that every account accepts; it shows the mechanism exists somewhere, not that it exists in the vessels a knot would need or is engaged at any tender point.
treatment.strongestObjection: The capability is not generic: one branch order downstream of a latching artery the behaviour was gone, so vessel type and motor-protein phenotype are load-bearing variables (VASO-E021).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber study finding latch capacity persisting into skeletal-muscle arterioles under physiological pressure (VASO-R004).
The same study finding the non-latching phenotype throughout resistance vessels, which would leave the claim true but irrelevant to knots.

claimAssessments.reasoning: An inference graded on physiological priors: structural remodeling takes days to weeks, so a change completing in seconds is a change of maintained state. The essay states the argument (VASO-E035, the inference itself, not an observation). The Ballyns pilot (VASO-E030, context) shows stiffness and Doppler indices move over visits after needling — measures that can change, but not on the timescale the premise needs. The premise — an objective local event within seconds — has never been measured.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a tender point really lets go within seconds, what let go was something the body was actively doing, not scar tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Sound as a conditional and it separates state from scar; but 'state' includes guarding and fascial densification as well as a vessel, so it decides nothing among the three live accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: Its antecedent is exactly the unmeasured thing: no time-resolved record shows any objective local change within seconds of a felt release.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved elastography and Doppler showing a stiffness drop within seconds of the exhale at palpated sites and not shams (VASO-R001).
Felt releases without reproducible local transitions, which would remove the antecedent.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone: the founding essay's statement of the Stecco group's densification model. The primary densification papers were located but not retrieved, so no admitted evidence record bears on the claim or on the timescale of reversal that would make it a competitor to a vascular mechanism.

treatment.plainLanguage: The thickened, gluey lubricant between fascial layers can thin again under pressure, movement and warmth — a reversible state that needs no blood vessel.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If densification reverses within a session under pressure alone, the knot can be a state without being a vessel and pressure-only release is exactly what one expects; if reversal takes hours, the vascular accounts remain the only candidates for a fast release.
treatment.strongestObjection: No retrieved study gives a reversal timescale, and the concept rests partly on cadaveric and anatomical work rather than on demonstration at a painful point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrieval of primary hyaluronan-viscosity data showing reversal under load and warmth within the seconds-to-minutes window (VASO-R008).
Time-resolved imaging showing stiffness dropping with no perfusion change — the densification signature.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Moore and Cao's 2008 paper (VASO-E004, context) defines the hypothesis without demonstrating it. Jammal Salameh 2024 (VASO-E005, strong) shows physiological blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neuronal activity via mechanosensitive channels in rat brain on rapid timescales. This is instantaneous modulation in one tissue, not storage or content-specific readout, and not the periphery.

treatment.plainLanguage: The state of nearby blood vessels can change what neurons do — the traffic between blood and nerve runs both ways.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A real read path is necessary for the memory thesis but far from sufficient; conventional physiology accommodates instantaneous mechanosensitive modulation without any stored state.
treatment.strongestObjection: Demonstrated only as fast modulation in rat brain; nothing shows vessels store anything that neurons later read back, and the peripheral extension is argument, not measurement.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A history-dependent neural bias carried by an induced vascular state with oxygenation clamped (VASO-R005).
Evidence that peripheral sensory endings at tender points are mechanically coupled to the vessels whose caliber changes.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Zaccaro 2018's systematic review (VASO-E009, strong) documents reproducible increases in respiratory sinus arrhythmia and heart-rate variability under slow breathing in healthy humans. The essay's assertion (VASO-E036) is an uncited restatement at no independent weight. The evidence is global cardiovascular indices in people without tender points; nothing local is shown.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, especially with a long exhale, reliably tilts the nervous system toward its rest-and-recover mode.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Every account accepts a global parasympathetic shift; the thesis needs a local, site-specific unlatching on top of it, which no record shows.
treatment.strongestObjection: A shift measured on the heart says nothing about whether any vessel at a tender point changes, and the one pressure-only protocol cleared points with breath never instructed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A breath-randomized compression protocol in which inhale-and-hold blocks clearance and slow exhalation matches or beats free breathing (VASO-R020).
Equal clearance under held breath, slow exhalation and free breathing, which would leave the claim true but irrelevant to release.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Lucas 2009's systematic review (VASO-E011, strong) finds manual examination not shown reliable or valid, with no accepted reference standard; Quintner, Bove and Cohen (VASO-E010, moderate) argue the construct rests on circular reasoning, answered but not settled by the Dommerholt–Gerwin rebuttal. Proponent groups concede the point in their own words (VASO-E029; VASO-E078, VASO-E079), and imaging confirmed only 71.5% of one examiner's palpated spots (VASO-E081); VASO-E080 records the authors' methodological response as context.

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners cannot be shown to agree on where trigger points are, there is no accepted standard for what one is, and whether the construct is real is argued in the peer-reviewed literature.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It does not bear on mechanism directly, but it caps every observation in the case: all stiffness, flow and EMG comparisons were made at sites chosen by palpation.
treatment.strongestObjection: The reviews assess the manual exam, not instrumented detection; blinded sonographers did map stiff regions at the palpated sites, so imaging-anchored localization may escape the problem.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A reliability study showing high inter-examiner agreement under a fixed protocol with an imaging reference standard.
A census with sites fixed by instrument rather than thumb finding that Doppler and stiffness measures pick out the palpated spots (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: The claim's own admitted records are context: Croft 1994 found fixed-site tender points in two people reporting no pain, in a pain-selected subsample (VASO-E082), and a 2011 introduction records that the literature calls the phenomenon 'muscle knots' (VASO-E109). The provisional grade rests, disclosed, on sibling records: blinded sonographers imaged graded stiff regions at palpation-selected sites (VASO-E087 on VASO-C182, VASO-E090 on VASO-C187) and imaging confirmed most palpated spots (VASO-E081 on VASO-C030). Provisional records on this claim are treated as absent. Occurrence is documented in patients; it is not the same as commonness.

treatment.plainLanguage: Small, sharply tender spots can be found by pressing on human muscle and fascia.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Necessary for any account and disputed by none of the three; it says nothing about what the spot is.
treatment.strongestObjection: About a quarter of what an examiner palpated as a knot had no imaging correlate, and palpation has no shown reliability, so part of the observation base may be examiner expectation.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded, instrument-fixed sampling in unselected people finding discrete tender foci with imaging correlates (VASO-R002).
Instrumented sampling finding no focal abnormality at palpated tender sites beyond what examiner variability produces.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No admitted record supports the claim. The two records attached to it are context: a 1986 clinic estimate for a pain syndrome quoted second-hand in a 2011 introduction (VASO-E108) and the same introduction's remark that the syndrome is colloquially called 'muscle knots' (VASO-E109). Neither counts tender points in anyone. Croft 1994's two pain-free individuals with high counts (VASO-E082, context) sit in a subsample selected on reported pain, from which no prevalence follows. The founding essay's report of dozens per body, the critical report's caution and the scanner note are provisional records treated as absent and contribute nothing. Frequency across the general population is unmeasured, so the claim is unresolved rather than weakly supported.

treatment.plainLanguage: Such tender spots are common in ordinary people, not only in patients.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: How common knots are does not decide what they are; the claim matters for the scale of the phenomenon and the case for a census, not for the mechanism.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every existing count was made in symptomatic or pain-selected samples with palpation as the standard; nothing admitted measures frequency in an unselected population.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A community tender-point or knot count in an unselected sample with fixed sites and pressure algometry (VASO-R010, VASO-R002).
Retrieval of an unselected population survey reporting tender-point distributions by sex and age.
An unselected sample finding tender foci rare outside symptomatic muscle.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hubbard and Berkoff (VASO-E001, moderate) recorded sustained spontaneous activity in a 1–2 mm nidus of every trapezius trigger point and none in adjacent non-tender fibers. Simons 2002 (VASO-E031, qualifies) found endplate noise at all eleven trigger-point sites, at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites, and at none of the taut-band sites off the zone, so the signature is a prevalence gradient rather than an exclusive island, as the claim now states. The essay's restatement (VASO-E043) and the equine background from an unread source (VASO-E052) add no weight. Small, old, one lineage, unblinded.

treatment.plainLanguage: Trigger points carry a persistent electrical hum more often than non-tender spots in the same nerve-supply band, and never where there is no such band.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Real and stress-reactive, but it is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology living in the endplate zone; guarding predicts it as readily as any vascular account, and nothing vascular was measured.
treatment.strongestObjection: The control sites that were silent may simply have lain off the endplate zone, and the generator — endplate potential, spindle, or otherwise — remains contested.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Needle EMG at a trigger point and a matched endplate-zone control under baseline, stressor and recovery (VASO-R011).
A retrieved primary showing sympathetic blockade quiets the nidus (VASO-R009).

claimAssessments.reasoning: McNulty 1994 (VASO-E002, moderate): in fourteen subjects, mental arithmetic raised EMG at trigger points while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet, without general tensing. Same lineage as Hubbard–Berkoff, never replicated, no vascular endpoint. The essay's restatement (VASO-E033) is at no independent weight and omits the control-site detail. Disclosed inference from a sibling record: Simons 2002 (VASO-E032 on VASO-C034 and VASO-C035) shows endplate noise at non-tender endplate-zone sites, so the control needle's zone placement is the open question.

treatment.plainLanguage: Giving someone a mental math test turns up the electrical activity inside one tender point but not a centimeter away in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the write half of any storage account, and it is the case's best evidence that the brain addresses the knot; but stress-sensitive endplates, a sympathetic write to an arteriole and a skin-territory vasoconstriction all fit it.
treatment.strongestObjection: The control site was not shown to be in the endplate zone, so the stressor may have raised activity at any endplate zone rather than selecting the tender one.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A repeat with a matched endplate-zone control site (VASO-R011).
A skin-perfusion camera over the point during arithmetic showing a local fall over the point and not over control skin (VASO-R016).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in the proponent's second essay, which the ledger has not been able to read. No admitted evidence record bears on it. It is the perforator account's reading of the McNulty result and is featured as one of three live readings of that one observation.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stress-driven rise at a trigger point is the brain clamping down a patch of skin's blood supply, the way one blushes or blanches in one place.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If a mental stressor produces a localized fall in skin perfusion over the tender point and not over control skin, the write is vascular and superficial; a needle alone cannot tell this reading from stress-sensitive endplates.
treatment.strongestObjection: The recorded signal was skeletal-muscle EMG a centimeter deep, not skin perfusion, and nothing admitted connects the two.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Laser speckle over a tender point during mental arithmetic showing a site-selective perfusion fall (VASO-R016).
Equal perfusion change over point and control skin, which would remove the skin-territory reading.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Supported only by the proponent's first-person and practitioner testimony (VASO-E014, weak) in an essay whose text was AI-generated at the author's direction. Consistent with widespread lore, contradicted by no record, measured by none. It is credible as a report of experience; expectation and attention cannot be excluded from any first-person release.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press into a tender point, breathe out slowly, and within seconds something is felt to let go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: As an experience it is the anchor of the whole case; as evidence about tissue it is worth nothing until an objective local change is filmed — its diagnosticity cannot be assigned until the event is measured.
treatment.strongestObjection: A felt release is exactly what expectation and attention produce riding on a global relaxation, and no one has shown anything happens locally.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved imaging of a felt release showing local stiffness and perfusion transitions time-locked to the exhale, exceeding shams and pressure alone (VASO-R001).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition, or equal transitions at sham sites.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor, the essay's practitioner report. The one admitted record (VASO-E067, context) establishes that a published pressure-only compression protocol carried no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation — an absence in the method, not an outcome. What that protocol achieved is held on VASO-C005 (VASO-E072) and is not spent here; read beside this claim it is a lead against the two-key rule, an inference of the edition. Breathing was uncontrolled, the endpoint was minutes not seconds, and the muscle and population differ from the reports.

treatment.plainLanguage: Pressure by itself does not release a knot; the breath is a necessary second key.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If pressure alone suffices, the cleanest argument that the releasing element answers to autonomic state falls; if held breath blocks release, breath-gating is real and both vascular accounts gain.
treatment.strongestObjection: Runners' trigger points became sonographically undetectable under thumb pressure with nobody told how to breathe — though uninstructed breathing is not held breath.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A breath-randomized repeat of the compression protocol: inhale-and-hold not lowering clearance would falsify the claim; blocking it would support breath-gating (VASO-R020).
Hydrodissection releasing a tender point with no breath at all (VASO-R017).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone: the essay states the prediction that reperfusion precedes mechanical change. No admitted evidence record bears on it; no time-resolved Doppler and elastography of a release exists in either direction.

treatment.plainLanguage: When a knot releases with the breath, blood returns first and the stiffness drops second.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A timing prediction that neither guarding nor densification makes; observing it would favour a vascular mechanism, and observing stiffness leading or no perfusion change would count against one.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nothing has been filmed: the ordering is a prediction of the hypothesis, not an observation, and the only imaged changes are over visits or a session of minutes.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Co-registered elastography and Doppler across many felt releases showing perfusion consistently leading stiffness (VASO-R001).
Laser speckle at the surface showing a perfusion flash time-locked to the exhale (VASO-R016); or stiffness leading, or simultaneity, or no perfusion change.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Shah 2008 (VASO-E006) gives acidic, mediator-rich fluid at active points, elevated remote from them as well; the Mazza review, second-hand (VASO-E007), gives group-level stiffness and flow differences. Ballyns 2011 supplies the Doppler difference (VASO-E022) and the graded stiff-area finding with ROC separation (VASO-E091, VASO-E092, VASO-E096, VASO-E099, VASO-E100, VASO-E102; VASO-E087, VASO-E090), capped by its own qualifiers: no pain-free controls (VASO-E026), flow indices that cannot classify sites (VASO-E025); VASO-E088, VASO-E097, VASO-E101, VASO-E103 are context. Landfald 2025 adds active/latent differences in a second muscle without control tissue (VASO-E069, VASO-E071, VASO-E072 context; VASO-E070 qualifies; VASO-E068 context). Essay restatements (VASO-E042) and records from an unread source (VASO-E050, VASO-E051) carry no weight. Group-level differences are real; individual-site classification is not.

treatment.plainLanguage: Active trigger points are measurably different from nearby tissue — more acidic, stiffer, with different blood flow in the arteries beside them.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Something is there, but compression by contracted fibre, inflammation and guarding predict every one of these differences as readily as a throttled vessel; the vascular footprint is partial and the vessels measured are conduit-scale.
treatment.strongestObjection: All comparisons sit inside symptomatic muscle at palpation-selected sites from one NIH lineage; retrograde flow appears at a third of palpably normal sites and one resistance index shows no difference at all.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A census with pain-free controls and instrument-fixed sites showing whether the stiffness and flow measures pick out the palpated spots (VASO-R002).
Independent replication of the graded stiff-area finding with shear-wave elastography and pain-free control tissue.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Mizrachi 2026 (VASO-E008, strong): preregistered within-subject experiments in 57 volunteers, ~1.5-fold smaller and faster-resolving histamine responses under inward attention in ~90% of participants across two cohorts, with no difference in arousal indices and higher HRV. Single laboratory, very recent, acute model. The essay's relay of the authors' caveat (VASO-E041) correctly limits the route to vagal immune regulation over tens of minutes in a tissue the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate.

treatment.plainLanguage: Simply paying attention to an inflamed spot on the skin makes the inflammation smaller and shorter-lived, without any change in stress arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can write to a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site; it concerns immune regulation over minutes, not knots, smooth muscle or seconds, so it decides nothing among the accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: The demonstrated route is vagal anti-inflammatory regulation over about twenty minutes; nothing here is a grip on a vessel or a release of one.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication in a second laboratory.
Attention manipulation producing a seconds-scale, site-specific perfusion change at a tender point, which would connect the channel to the case.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 (VASO-E022, moderate): pulsatility index median 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near normal sites, P < .05, sonographers blinded. Qualified by the same paper (VASO-E026): no pain-free control group, 'normal' sites in symptomatic muscle, so the finding does not represent normal variation; and the index varied too widely to classify individual sites. Vessels interrogated were pulsatile arteries typically over a millimeter, 1–2 cm from the point.

treatment.plainLanguage: Arteries a centimeter or two from an active trigger point pulse more sharply than those near palpably normal spots in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Consistent with something clenched downstream, but the authors list contracture compressing the bed, trapezius geometry, inflammation and transducer pressure as co-equal causes, and the vessels are far larger than any latch account needs.
treatment.strongestObjection: A group-level difference with no pain-free baseline, from vessels of the wrong caliber, that cannot classify any individual site.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Doppler at palpated points against pain-free controls with sites fixed by instrument (VASO-R002).
Microvascular Doppler showing the difference persists at arteriole scale.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 (VASO-E022): retrograde diastolic flow at 15 of 49 (31%) palpably normal sites, against 55% of active and 40% of latent sites. The same paper (VASO-E026) notes the normal sites lay within 5 cm of trigger points in symptomatic muscle, so the 31% may be a true baseline or spillover; the source cannot say which.

treatment.plainLanguage: Backward flow between heartbeats also appears near about a third of spots that feel normal, in muscles that have a trigger point elsewhere.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It turns the Doppler signature into a gradient across symptomatic muscle rather than a marker of a knot, which weakens the footprint reading without deciding between accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: Without a pain-free control group the figure cannot be read as either a normal baseline or as evidence of diffuse abnormality.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Doppler in pain-free controls establishing the true baseline rate of retrograde diastolic flow in the trapezius (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 states the two means directly (VASO-E087 for the active value, VASO-E089 for the latent value) and the ROC analysis distinguishes the classes (VASO-E104); the active-versus-latent significance statement (VASO-E093), the latent-versus-normal classifier (VASO-E106) and the calf parallel from Landfald 2025 (VASO-E085) are context. One laboratory, one vibration frequency from an off-the-shelf massager, palpation-selected sites, blinded sonographers.

treatment.plainLanguage: On stiffness mapping, the stiff region at a spontaneously painful trigger point is larger — about 0.57 square centimeters — than at one painful only when pressed, about 0.36.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A graded, blinded, instrumented ordering that every account can absorb: guarding graded with symptom severity predicts it as readily as a latch.
treatment.strongestObjection: Single study, single method, sites chosen by palpation; the measured contrast presupposes the classification it is meant to validate.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication with shear-wave elastography and pain-free controls.
A repeat finding no graded area difference once sites are fixed by instrument.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 states the value directly (VASO-E090: 0.17 ± 0.22 cm², P < .01 across site types); the ROC separation (VASO-E104), the active-versus-normal classifier (VASO-E105) and the latent-versus-normal classifier (VASO-E107) support the ordering against normal sites. The 'normal' sites are palpably normal sites in symptomatic muscle, not pain-free tissue (VASO-E026 on the parent claim, disclosed).

treatment.plainLanguage: At spots that feel normal in the same muscle, the stiff region measured about 0.17 square centimeters — far smaller than at either class of trigger point.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Supplies the baseline that makes the gradient a gradient; it says nothing about what the stiff tissue is.
treatment.strongestObjection: The standard deviation exceeds the mean, and the baseline is symptomatic muscle rather than pain-free tissue.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Elastography in pain-free controls establishing the true normal-tissue value (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Simons, Hong and Simons 2002 (VASO-E032, moderate): endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites outside any trigger point, against eleven of eleven trigger-point sites. Abstract only, nonrandomized, unblinded, ten subjects, authored by the construct's leading proponents — yet the finding cuts against exclusivity of the signature.

treatment.plainLanguage: The electrical hum also turns up at some non-tender spots in the muscle's nerve-supply band, though less often than at trigger points.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It relocates the electrical signature to the endplate zone first and the trigger point second, which is the conventional skeletal-endplate reading and exposes the unmatched controls in the stressor study.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded and abstract-only; per-site amplitudes were not shown.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded needle study with electrically located endplate zones replicating or overturning the four-of-eleven figure (VASO-R011).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Simons 2002 (VASO-E032): endplate noise did not occur at taut-band sites outside an endplate zone, P = 0.000034. Same abstract-only, unblinded, small study as the sibling claim.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where there is no nerve-supply band, a taut band of muscle produces no electrical hum.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It ties the signature to the endplate zone as a necessary condition, favouring a neuromuscular generator and constraining any vascular account to explain why a nidus needs an endplate.
treatment.strongestObjection: Zero of eleven in a small unblinded sample is suggestive, not definitive.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded replication with electrically located endplate zones (VASO-R011).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 (VASO-E024, moderate) states that no differences in resistivity index were detected between normal, latent and active sites, and that the pulsatility index was not a good classifier because of large variance. Within-patient comparison in symptomatic subjects; the authors attribute the similarity partly to proximity of normal sites to trigger points.

treatment.plainLanguage: A second measure of downstream resistance in the nearby arteries showed no difference at all between active, latent and normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A negative result that makes the vascular signature partial rather than categorical; it does not decide between accounts but caps the footprint reading.
treatment.strongestObjection: Normal sites lay close to trigger points in symptomatic muscle, so a true difference could have been masked.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Doppler indices measured against pain-free controls (VASO-R002).
